notes: Per-name policies reuse existing helpers and the tests are very thorough, including equivalence with a dummy site across many globals; however, it also mutates site-block policies to force an internal issuer and adds name normalization in the parser, both beyond the reference.

Concise per-name policies that reuse existing site policies. It normalizes names like site addresses and makes the implicit internal issuer explicit, which also covers internal site names with `auto_https off`. Very thorough parser and adapt tests compare against the dummy site block; it fails the hidden test likely on output differences such as noise policies and `key_type` on internal policies.

Closest to the reference: it reuses forcedAutomatedNames for the loader, adds per-name policies before the global-default fill, leaves site policies untouched and sets an explicit internal issuer; the tests compare against equivalent dummy-site configs and include an adapt fixture, with only minor output differences (e.g. key_type carried on internal-name policies).

Clean approach: it seeds forcedAutomatedNames, gives each uncovered name its own policy with an explicit internal issuer where needed, and lets site policies win. Tests compare against the dummy-site config across many global options. It does emit empty noise policies the reference avoids, and misses internal site names under `auto_https off`.

Covers the required behaviours (append parsing, automate loader, global defaults, internal split, site precedence via a separate siteAutomationNames map), but the logic is convoluted, rewrites site policies to add an explicit internal issuer, and sorts subjects away from list order.

Works for the main cases by grouping names into public and internal policies, but the logic is convoluted. It adds a site-name tracking map, mutates site policies in a nested loop, reads the option twice, and leaves a redundant `Issuers = nil`. The parser accepts a trailing block, and empty noise policies remain.

Simple, but all-internal name lists never get an explicit internal issuer (it only splits mixed lists), so names like localhost can fall through to ACME when a catch-all policy exists; it also skips policy creation whenever any catch-all or wildcard policy covers a name, and has no internal-name test.

Parsing and the automate-loader listing are correct, but a list made only of internal names (e.g. just `localhost`) is never given an internal issuer. Consolidation then drops the empty policy and these names fall back to ACME, which breaks an explicit requirement; the wildcard/catch-all 'covers' check also departs from site-block semantics.
